video_goal: Demonstrate how to guide a child in tying their Stride Rite sneakers using the visual 'bunny ears' two-loop method.
required_subjects_and_props: Child, adult guide, Stride Rite sneakers with standard laces

outline_steps.visual_action: Adult hands place a colorful Stride Rite sneaker on a child's foot, pulling the two loose shoelaces straight out to the sides.
Adult hands gently guide the child's small hands to grip one shoelace end in each fist.
The child's hands cross the left shoelace over the right shoelace, laying them flat against the shoe to form an 'X'.
The child's fingers tuck the top lace under the 'X' and pull both ends outward to tighten the base knot against the shoe tongue.
The child's left hand pinches the middle of the left lace and folds it in half, creating the first 'bunny ear' loop.
The child's right hand pinches the middle of the right lace and folds it in half, creating the second 'bunny ear' loop.
The child holds both loops upright side-by-side, with the Stride Rite logo visible on the shoe tongue just below the hands.
The child's hands cross the right loop over the left loop, forming a new 'X' shape with the folded laces.
An adult index finger enters the frame and taps the small triangular gap formed at the bottom of the crossed loops.
The child's thumb and forefinger push the tip of the top loop down and completely through the triangular gap.
The child's hands grasp the tops of both loops and pull them outward in opposite directions simultaneously.
The child pats the finished, tightened double-loop knot resting securely on the Stride Rite sneaker.
